extracted.intended_audience: U.S. biomedical engineers applying for Whitaker International Fellows and Scholars awards (applicants and their institutional nominators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for U.S. biomedical engineers applying (via institutional nomination) to the Whitaker International Fellows and Scholars Program for international research and educational placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must: Be highly qualified; Have demonstrated significant achievement in research, education, or other societal activity related to biomedical engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a baseline eligibility/merit filter — reviewers look for demonstrated accomplishments in research, education or societal activity related to biomedical engineering rather than vague potential alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy between career goals and proposed overseas experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should demonstrate synergy between career goals and the proposed overseas experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must clearly connect the overseas project to their long-term career trajectory; proposals that do not show this alignment risk being viewed as disconnected or irrelevant to professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / Residency Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be U.S. citizens or have U.S. permanent residency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard eligibility requirement — non-U.S. citizens/permanent residents are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be nominated by the Dean of a School or Chair of the biomedical engineering department at their current or most recent degree granting institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are not self-submitted; institutional endorsement via a nominated process is mandatory and reflects institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Must have language ability to carry out the proposed project in the host country at the time of departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate sufficient language skills for research and daily functioning in host environment; lack of language ability may undermine project feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitaker Fellows (Junior) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Biomedical engineers ranging from graduating seniors to those conducting doctoral studies; Should have a BS or MS degree in biomedical engineering or a closely related field; Designed to enhance and accelerate career trajectories of future leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets early-career applicants (senior undergrads, MS, PhD students). Emphasize potential and how the award will accelerate emergence as a leader in academic/industrial/governmental/clinical roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitaker Scholars (Senior) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Biomedical engineers who have/will have a PhD by the beginning date of their awards; Should have a degree in biomedical engineering AND a doctorate (not more than three years prior to the start of the grant) OR will receive the PhD prior to the start of the grant; Designed to enable PhD-holding researchers to lay foundations for international collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets early-career post-PhD researchers (within ~3 years of degree). Demonstrate readiness to establish sustainable international research collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: References requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Three references required; Recommended that all references be from academics or professionals in biomedical engineering or a closely-related field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference letters should speak to achievements, potential, and fit for international research; choosing recommenders within biomedical engineering or closely-related fields is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Letter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Whitaker Program requires a letter of support from the host affiliation as part of the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substantive host letter that confirms support, resources, and mentorship expectations strengthens feasibility and host quality evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed plan for proposed activities; Justification for chosen host institution; Demonstration of how project advances candidate's career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project descriptions should include methods/activities, clear rationale for host choice, feasibility details, and explicit linkage to career development; vague or generic project plans weaken competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: Career trajectory; Why this international experience; Long-term goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statements must narrate professional development, explain why international training is essential now, and articulate the intended long-term impact on the applicant's career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Candidate (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic record; Research accomplishments; Leadership potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the candidate's prior achievements and capacity to benefit from and contribute to the international experience; evidence of leadership and a strong academic/research track record is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Proposed Project (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific/technical merit; Feasibility; Potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are evaluated for intellectual merit, realistic scope and methods, and the likelihood of producing meaningful outcomes for the candidate and the field; infeasible or low-impact projects score poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Host Affiliation (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation of host institution; Mentorship plan; Resources available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong host institutions with clear mentorship plans and adequate resources materially increase project success; the host letter should substantiate these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Value (evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment with candidate's career goals; Potential to broaden the field of biomedical engineering; International collaboration value; Cultural exchange dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond technical merit, reviewers consider broader strategic contributions: how the experience fosters international collaborations, broadens the field, and supports cultural exchange tied to the applicant's career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Strategic Consideration — Novelty of Host Opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a host that provides genuinely new opportunities (not extensions of current work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that simply continue existing research at a new location are discouraged; emphasize novel skills, perspectives, methods, or collaborations the host uniquely provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Strategic Consideration — Cultural and intellectual readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate cultural and intellectual readiness for international experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show preparedness to work in the host cultural/intellectual environment, including prior experience, language preparation, or plans for adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Strategic Consideration — Justify host and country choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate why this specific host and country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit reasons the chosen institution and country are optimal for the project's goals; generic host choices weaken strategic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Strategic Consideration — Field-advancing impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how experience advances biomedical engineering field broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the prospective contributions to the wider discipline (methods, collaborations, dissemination) rather than narrowly personal benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-month to multi-year placements; Living stipends, travel, project support; Benefits package varies by award type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan budgets and timelines consistent with award types; clarify requested support and how it will enable proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Required final report on impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must submit a final report describing outcomes and impact; applicants should consider how they will document and measure impact during the project.
